statement.text:
Let G = a, b | ap = (ab)3 = b2 = (aσ ba2/σ b)2 = 1 , where p is a prime, σ is
an integer not divisible by p. The group P SL2 (p) is a factor-group of G so that there
is a short exact sequence 1 → N → G → P SL2 (p) → 1. For each p > 2 there is σ
such that N = 1, for example, σ = 4. Let N ab denote the factor-group of N by its
commutator subgroup. It is known that for some p there is σ such that N ab is infinite
(for example, for p = 41 one can take σ 2 ≡ 2 (mod 41)), whereas for some other p (for
example, for p = 43) the group N ab is finite for every σ.
    a) Is the set of primes p for which N ab is finite for every σ infinite?
    b) Is there an arithmetic condition on σ which ensures that N ab is finite?
                                                                              J. Mennicke
